top.title: U-17 WWC: How we overcame opening defeat to win title – Oluebube
top.description: Nigeria’s Flamingos forward, Oluebube Umejiaku, has explained how the team recovered from their opening defeat to Poland to win the 2026 FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup in Morocco. Nigeria began their campaign with a 2-1 loss to Poland, despite Umejiaku scoring as a substitute. However, the team bounced back, treating every subsequent fixture as a final on their way to winning the competition. The Flamingos defeated DPR Korea, Mexico and other opponents before overcoming Japan 2-1 in Saturday’s final to claim the trophy. Umejiaku, who started the tournament on the bench, became one of Nigeria’s standout performers, scoring crucial goals, including in the final, and winning the Golden Ball award as the tournament’s best player. Speaking to FIFA.com after Nigeria’s historic triumph, she said the players were determined to change their fortunes following the opening loss to Poland. “When we lost the first game against Poland, everybody said we needed to wake up because we didn’t come here to look at anybody’s face and we have to take every game as a final. We don’t downgrade anything; we play and we put all our best into every game.” Umejiaku also reflected on her journey from a substitute to one of the tournament’s most influential players, saying she remained hopeful of getting an opportunity to start. “Every time I went to training and every time I slept, I told God that I’m praying for all the people that are starting. But when I wanted to start, I just told God that it is my time,” she said. Another key contributor to Nigeria’s triumph was Awawu Bashiru, who initially had limited playing time under head coach Akeem Busari. Bashiru played just 77 minutes between the opening match and the quarter-final against Venezuela before earning her first start against Brazil. She scored twice in that encounter and also opened the scoring in the final against Japan. Reflecting on the team’s achievement, Bashiru credited their success to teamwork and the technical crew’s instructions. “I’m so happy, I’m so excited and I’m so grateful,” she said. “The teamwork, instruction and listening to our coaches is why we got the goals and why we won the final. We are history-makers. We made Nigeria, and the millions of people there, proud.” Busari, meanwhile, explained that his decisions to change the starting line-up were based on the players’ attitude, character and commitment rather than reputation. “No matter how good you are, I’m a coach that plays on character,” Busari said of making those key changes. “It’s all about mindset, attitude and merit; if they’re there, you get your playing time. If they’re not there, you’re waiting to come in. As a coach, we want everyone to wire up and play together.” Nigeria’s victory made the country the first African nation to win the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup and the first from the continent to claim a women’s FIFA tournament title. top.title: Israeli president Herzog picks Eisenkot to form new government
top.description: Israeli President Isaac Herzog has chosen opposition leader and former military chief, Gadi Eisenkot, to form a new government following an election that left both his camp and Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s coalition short of a parliamentary majority. Herzog’s office announced on Saturday night that the president had informed Eisenkot, leader of the Yashar party, of his intention to give him the mandate to form a government. The formal appointment is expected to take place at a ceremony at the president’s residence in Jerusalem on Sunday. “This is the time to establish a national emergency government. I will do anything possible to prove us worthy,” Eisenkot wrote on X following the announcement. The decision brings Eisenkot closer to replacing Netanyahu, Israel’s longest-serving prime minister, after the religious-nationalist coalition lost its parliamentary majority in the October 27 election. Netanyahu’s camp secured 54 seats in the 120-member parliament, while Eisenkot’s opposition bloc won 48, leaving both short of the 61 seats required to form a government. During consultations with Herzog, Eisenkot received endorsements from two Arab-majority political lists, whose support could prove crucial in the coalition-building process. However, uncertainty remains over whether Eisenkot’s bloc would accept a formal alliance with the Arab-led parties, particularly after more than three years of war in Gaza. Netanyahu has opposed any arrangement involving the Arab parties, accusing them of supporting terrorism and warning against forming a government with what he described as “terrorist supporters”. He has also called for a national unity government. Eisenkot, however, has indicated a willingness to work with Arab-led parties under certain conditions, including their acceptance that Hamas is a terrorist organisation that must be dismantled. He has also pledged to take action against extremist Israeli settlers in the occupied West Bank accused of attacking Palestinians, describing the incidents as “Jewish terror” allegedly enabled by Netanyahu’s government. Despite his willingness to engage with Arab-led parties, Eisenkot opposes the creation of a Palestinian state. He has also vowed to end Hamas’ rule in Gaza and destroy its military wing. Eisenkot served as Israel’s Chief of General Staff from 2015 to 2019 and commanded the military during the 2006 war with Hezbollah. During the conflict, he developed the so-called “Dahiya doctrine”, a military strategy advocating the use of overwhelming force against civilian infrastructure in areas controlled by Hezbollah. Under the Israeli constitutional process, Eisenkot has 28 days to secure the support of at least 61 lawmakers and form a government. Herzog can grant him an additional 14 days if he fails to meet the deadline. If Eisenkot cannot secure a parliamentary majority within the allotted period, the president may offer the mandate to another candidate. Failure by any candidate to form a government

top.title: WIMBIZ pushes for more women in business, leadership through mentorship
top.description: By Enitan Abdultawab The Women in Management, Business and Public Service (WIMBIZ) has renewed its push for greater participation of women in business and leadership, identifying mentorship, visibility and empowerment as key tools for helping women access opportunities and advance their careers. The Executive Head of WIMBIZ, Omowunmi Akingbohungbe, said the organisation was committed to inspiring and empowering women to attain leadership positions while equipping them to become entrepreneurs. Speaking during an interview at the organisation’s 25th annual conference in Lagos, Akingbohungbe said WIMBIZ connects experienced and accomplished women with emerging leaders to guide them through the challenges of building careers and businesses. “We’re big on mentoring. We connect mentors, accomplished and experienced women with rising leaders so they can handhold them and show them the path so they’re not reinventing the wheel,” she said. She also stressed the importance of visibility, noting that women needed to make their abilities known, develop confidence and put themselves forward for leadership opportunities. According to her, many women often hold back from applying for leadership positions because they feel they are not qualified, whereas men are more likely to take the chance. “Most times women will think I’m not qualified and all of that, but men would apply. And we also have the potential,” she said. Akingbohungbe said WIMBIZ was therefore working to ensure women recognise their capabilities and have the confidence to pursue opportunities in business and public service. “At WIMBIZ, we train, mentor, empower women. We give women a right to be entrepreneurs at the same time,” she added. She described the organisation’s partnership with Autos, its official automobile partner for the annual conference, as part of its 25th anniversary celebrations. She said the partnership would also provide discounts to WIMBIZ members and free vehicle servicing for two years. The 25th annual conference was held under the theme, “Rooted, Rising, Ready: Born in Africa, Built for the World.” The post WIMBIZ pushes for more women in business, leadership through mentorship appeared first on Vanguard News .

top.title: Bayern Munich not taking any guff from 1860 honks
top.description: (Photo by Leonhard Simon/Getty Images) | Getty Images The rivalry between Bayern Munich and 1860 Munich is never particularly short on hostility, but one incident during Bayern’s Bundesliga title celebrations at Marienplatz has now developed into a legal dispute that is showing no signs of slowing down. On May 17, as Bayern Munich celebrated another league title in front of thousands of supporters and live television cameras, supporters of local rivals 1860 Munich managed to smuggle an insulting banner into the event and unfurl it in the fan se ction. Bayern subsequently filed a criminal complaint against persons unknown for insult, with the club taking issue not only with the message but also with the use and defacement of its logo. The matter has now reached the home of one alleged participant. According to Bild , poli ce recently searched the apartment of a suspect believed to have been involved in the incident. Four detectives from the Munich Criminal Investigation Department carried out the search under an emergency warrant issued by the Munich District Court. Computers and other electronic devices were seized as investigator s looked for potential evidence, including receipts, bank transfers, and chat logs. Interestingly, Bild (via @iMiaSanMia ) re ports that the suspect’s lawyer described the officers as very friendly, claiming they even chuckled at the prank. That detail has not exactly helped make the investigation look less unusual from the defense’s perspective. Sebastian Wagner, a defense attorney who regularly represents 1860 Munich supporters in criminal proceedings, strongly disputes the legal basis for the case: “The behavior described doe s not constitute a criminal offense. FC Bayern AG is also not a collective entity that can be the victim of an insult.” Wagner is also unhappy that aut horities carried out a search in the first place, suggesting that Bayern’s influence may have played a role in the judiciary’s response: “You get the impression that FC Bayern says, ‘Jump,’ and the Munich judicia ry asks, ‘How high?’” Bayern Munich, however, has its own explanation for pursuing the matter. The club reportedly had two prim ary objectives. First, it wanted the derogatory banner handed over so that its logo would no longer remain in circulation in that form. Second, Bayern ultimately decided to take legal action because it does not tolerate its logo being defaced or disparaged, particularly out of a se nse of responsibility toward its supporters. And the accused supporter is apparently not interested in backing down. Speaking through his lawyer, the 1860 Munich fan delivered a response that sounds very much in keeping with the rivalry: “A derby lasts 90 minutes. But in court, I would also take on FC Bayern all the way into stoppage time.” Well, there is certainly no shortage of confidence on either side. top.title: 'I can't believe he is one of us' - inside Salah's life in Trabzon
top.description: Mohamed Salah has scored 10 goals in 15 games for Turkish club Trabzonspor [Getty Images] Back in August, when Mohamed Salah landed in Istanbul after flying in from his holiday in Mykonos, he wore Trabzonspor's burgundy and blue home strip as he stepped out of the plane to be greeted by thousands of fans. That kit sold out almost instantly. Later that day, as Salah headed to Trabzon in north-east Turkey to complete the formalities of one of the most unexpected transfers, he asked one of his entourage what he should wear. "The same kit," came the response, but Trabzonspor president Ertugrul Dogan advised Salah to wear the black away kit instead. Of course, that sold out too. From the outset of the 34-year-old's arrival to this historic port city on the Black Sea, that sense of adulation has only grown. "I went to the airport to see him in Istanbul and it was surreal," says Nisa Dumangoz. "I still can't believe that he is one of us." Go for a stroll through Trabzon on matchday and it is Salah's face which adorns everything. Even the walls inside the fishmongers have pictures of him. At the club shop in town, one of the staff jokes that the ground floor is for the Egyptian and the upper floor is for everything else. Outside the stadium, there are scarves, magnets, keyrings, lighters with his face on and Egyptian Nemes headdresses in Trabzonspor colours. Season ticket sales rocketed after his arrival. "Walking around Trabzon, it feels as though nine out of every 10 fans wearing a shirt have Salah's name on the back. The 10th has their own," says Turkish football journalist Hasan Tuncel. The club have surpassed their merchandise revenue from last year in three months since Salah's arrival, while the local airport is only getting busier. Liverpool was difficult to reach for many supporters across the Arab world and tickets were often hard to source. Trabzon is far more accessible, with new flights introduced from Cairo, Dubai and Riyadh since Salah's arrival. On our flight from Istanbul, we meet an Egyptian family of 10 coming from Cairo for Trabzonspor's Uefa Conference League game against Freiburg. "He is our ambassador and our Egyptian King, and with how many people want to come to Turkey now, he is their ambassador too," says Mahmoud. At the game, there is a group of Egyptian celebrities and influencers. A quick check of their social media shows their combined Instagram following of about five million. Trabzonspor have three million. Salah has 68 million. Salah recently went for a hike and posed for a picture on a rock in the Trabzon highlands. That rock has been renamed Salahtasi (Salah's Rock) and is now a tourist destination. The commercial element of his signing has more than been justified but crucially, on the pitch, Salah is driving Trabzonspor's push for the Turkish Super Lig title and he has hit the ground running with 10 goals and five assists in all competitions. top.title: Report: Liverpool will look to exploit a major weakness in Crystal Palace
top.description: Report: Liverpool will look to exploit a major weakness in Crystal Palace Crystal Palace v Liverpool: Away Form Meets Palace Pressure at Selhurst Park Crystal Palace arrive at this game in a state of anxiety, Liverpool arrive carrying irritation, and somewhere in that collision sits the shape of a compelling Premier League afternoon. According to BBC Football , this is a meeting between a home side sinking under the weight of grim numbers and an away side trying to prove that one bad week does not become a damaging trend. Palace’s predicament is stark. Pierre Sage has watched his team slide into the bottom three after a run that has stripped confidence and exposed weakness after weakness. The defeat to Tottenham offered a brutal snapshot of where they are. Jean-Philippe Mateta’s early dismissal wrecked the script, but what followed went beyond misfortune. Palace were overwhelmed in every department, pinned back, starved of possession and barely able to cross the halfway line with any purpose. Those figures matter because they fit a wider pattern. Palace have been conceding heavily, losing regularly and producing the kind of statistical profile that usually sends clubs towards relegation trouble. They have allowed far more shots than they have created themselves, and that imbalance is often a merciless judge over the long haul. When a team spends that much time defending, errors multiply, belief ebbs away and every opponent begins to sense vulnerability. Crystal Palace Struggles Laid Bare The most troubling part for Sage may be that the flaws are not subtle. Palace have become particularly susceptible in the air, with headed goals against them already mounting at an alarming rate. Defensive issues can often be dressed up as bad luck for a while, but repeated punishment from the same source points to a structural problem. Organisation, aggression and concentration all come into question. Yet football seldom respects neat scripts. Palace can still draw on a recent record against Liverpool that offers some encouragement. This fixture has become less one-sided than it once was, and Selhurst Park has provided them with resistance and reward in recent meetings. That does not erase current form, but it does suggest Liverpool will not be handed anything. Liverpool Away Form Offers Encouragement Liverpool, for their part, have reason to feel aggrieved by how the past few days have unfolded. Andoni Iraola began his reign with poise and momentum, yet successive defeats have checked the early glow. The loss to Fenerbahce was especially frustrating because of the manner of the goals conceded, all from set-pieces, and because it raised uncomfortable questions about control and concentration at key moments. IMAGO Iraola described those concessions as “cheap” and “messy”. He was equally agitated by the home defeat to Arsenal, a game in which Liverpool were not outclassed but still ended up making unwanted history by failing to register a shot on target at Anfield

top.description: Report: Spurs to make formal complaint after Leeds United defeat Tottenham to Lodge Formal Complaint After Mathys Tel Injury in Leeds Defeat Tottenham are preparing to make a formal complaint to Pro Ref after Jayden Bogle avoided a red card for the challenge that forced Mathys Tel off in the 1-0 loss to Leeds United. According to Standard , Spurs want clarity on why no dismissal followed despite a four-minute VAR review at Elland Road. The incident has quickly become the central talking point from a damaging afternoon for Roberto De Zerbi’s side. Bogle landed studs-up on Tel’s left Achilles, with the Tottenham forward attempting to continue before signalling that he could not carry on. He was later seen on crutches and in a protective boot, heightening concern over the severity of the problem. Mathys Tel injury concern grows There is now real anxiety inside Tottenham over the extent of the Mathys Tel injury. De Zerbi indicated after the match that further checks would follow, but the early outlook was troubling. The expectation is that the Frenchman could face a significant spell out, which would represent a major setback given his growing importance in the attack. Spurs also appear to feel the match turned at that point. Tel’s withdrawal disrupted their shape and threat, and Leeds gradually seized momentum before Noah Okafor scored the winner in the 79th minute. VAR decision leaves Spurs seeking answers The key issue for Tottenham is the process around the VAR decision. Bogle escaped any punishment, and Spurs now want an explanation from the officiating body as to how that conclusion was reached. In a game defined by fine margins, the sense at the club is that a serious challenge went insufficiently addressed. Photo IMAGO De Zerbi struck a measured tone afterwards, even after his own frustration on the touchline brought a yellow card and a touchline ban for the upcoming home match against Ipswich. He said, “No, I have big confidence in the referee.” He added, “Nothing changes if he goes to watch the clip or not. I think there was the VAR, and if they didn’t take the right decision, I don’t know. But we have confidence, we have to keep our eyes on the performance where we can improve.” Our View This is exactly the sort of episode that leaves people furious. A player ends up leaving on crutches and in a protective boot, there is a lengthy VAR review, and somehow nobody decides the challenge warrants even the strongest sanction available. It is very hard to square that with any claim of consistency. What makes it worse is that Tottenham then had to carry on without one of their most dangerous attacking options, and the entire flow of the game changed. That is the reality of these moments. top.title: Lionel Messi makes MLS history with back-to-back Golden Boot wins despite Decision Day blank
top.description: Lionel Messi makes MLS history with back-to-back Golden Boot wins despite Decision Day blank Lionel Messi has won the MLS Golden Boot for a second consecutive season, becoming the the first player in the league's history to win the award back to back. The Inter Miami captain ended the 2026 regular season on 26 goals, four clear of FC Dallas striker Petar Musa on 22. Nashville SC's Sam Surridge finished third with 21 goals, with Vancouver Whitecaps forward Brian White one further back. The crown arrived on a frustrating final day. Messi failed to score as Miami let a 3-0 home lead slip against Charlotte FC, settling for a 3-3 draw. Lionel Messi's numbers behind a second Golden Boot This year's tally fell short of the 29 goals Messi scored in 2025, which was the fourth-highest total ever recorded in a single MLS season. Carlos Vela holds the all-time record with 34 regular-season goals for Los Angeles FC in 2019. Messi's creative output also remained elite. He provided 17 assists, one fewer than league leader Pep Biel. The individual highlight of his campaign came in August, when he scored four times in a 7-1 rout of Montreal. Inter Miami turn to the MLS Cup defence Inter Miami now begin their bid to retain the MLS Cup, a feat no club has achieved since LA Galaxy in 2011/12. As the Eastern Conference's No. 2 seed, behind record-setting Nashville, they meet No. 7 Columbus Crew in a best-of-three first round. Messi is also chasing a third straight MLS MVP award. Before his repeat win last season, no player had ever won it in consecutive years, and Predrag Radosavljević (1997, 2003) was the only previous two-time winner. The award is voted on by media, players and club staff.

top.title: FIFA U-17 WWC: Why we lost to Nigeria in final – Japan coach Shirai
top.description: Japan U-17 women’s national team coach, Sadayoshi Shirai, has praised Nigeria’s Flamingos following his side’s 2-1 defeat in the final of the 2026 FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup in Morocco. Shirai admitted that Nigeria’s speed and physical strength posed major problems for his players, particularly when the Flamingos managed to break through their defence. Nigeria secured the title through goals from Oluebube Umejiaku and Awawu Bashiru, while Fuki Ito scored for Japan. Reacting after the encounter, Shirai acknowledged Nigeria’s superiority but maintained that his players gave their best throughout the final. “First of all, I have to say that Nigeria were a very strong team. We understood their strengths, but there were moments when they managed to get in behind our defence. Even so, I think our players fought incredibly hard until the very end, doing everything they could to cope with Nigeria’s speed and physical power. I also believe that if we had managed to score earlier, we might have had a better chance of winning the match. I want them [Japan’s players] to be proud of themselves. The way they fought until the very end of this World Cup will have inspired many people, and I hope they can take confidence from that,” Shirai said. Japan reached the final after defeating DPR Korea in the semi-finals, while Nigeria booked their place in the title decider with a victory over Brazil. The Flamingos eventually defeated Japan to claim the U-17 Women’s World Cup trophy, marking a historic achievement for Nigerian women’s football. The Jayhawks went up 32-26, and they just needed a stop against a struggling UCF offense to wrap things up. Luckily, for UCF, they had Alonza Barnett in at quarterback. He stayed cool, and marched the Knights down the field, and set them up with multiple shots at the endzone. One of those looked like a score, but was wiped out by replay. Then, as the clock was running out, UCF took another shot to tight end Caden Piening, who snagged the game-winner. Notably, however, the Big 12 officials took a very long look at the Piening touchdown. Seemingly, they wanted to find a way to overturn the call on the field. top.title: Arteta hails 'different' Noni Madueke as Arsenal winger responds to England snubs
top.description: Arteta hails 'different' Noni Madueke as Arsenal winger responds to England snubs Mikel Arteta believes Noni Madueke has returned as a 'different' player since deciding to train on his own during the last international break, and the Arsenal manager has now challenged the winger to go again. Madueke was Arsenal's main attacking outlet in Saturday's 1-0 win over Hull City. His stinging shot forced a save from Konstantinos Tzolakis, and Martin Odegaard followed up to score the only goal of the game. His 13 touches in the opposition box were the most by an Arsenal player in any Premier League game this season. Involved heavily throughout, no player had more dribbles (5) or more chances created and shots combined (8). Yet the 24-year-old left the pitch frustrated. Late on, Mikel Merino slipped him through, but his attempt to round Tzolakis clipped the goalkeeper's foot and the chance was gone. "He knew he had three clear chances to score," Arteta said. Noni Madueke's response to being left out Madueke started only two of Arsenal's first seven games this season and was not picked by Thomas Tuchel for England for last month's Nations League fixtures. Rather than sulk, Arteta revealed that he used the international break to train individually. The change since has been stark. He did not complete a full Premier League match last season, his first after joining from Chelsea in the summer of 2025. Since the break, he has played the full 90 minutes in four of Arsenal's five league games, and came off the bench at half-time in the other to curl in the winner against Nottingham Forest. He scored the opener in the Champions League in midweek against Slavia Prague, and Bukayo Saka's injury against Bayern Munich has moved him back to the right, where he is now central to Arteta's plans. However, despite that improved form and Saka's absence, he was again overlooked by England for the upcoming break. “It was a close call and a difficult decision not to bring Noni, because he got his minutes after Bukayo’s injury at Arsenal,” Tuchel said at a post-squad selection press conference at Wembley. “He got some goals. It was very close. But also [in that position], we stuck with the group that we had [during the last international break] and give them our trust.” Arteta made clear Madueke had to earn his chance. "But that's the second part of the story," he told reporters. "The first one is you need to earn the right to be able to do that. Noni did. He didn't do it in the first part of the season; that's why he wasn't playing. "But the way he reacted to that is a great example for the rest of the squad, which is: I want to do more. He went away, decided to train, came back, and he was a different Noni. You could sense that he meant business, and he wasn't going to accept that situation. Since then, he's been incredible. So now you are in that position, now you need to hold it and improve it, and he can still do that. So, let's see what he does in this break."

top.title: INEC to meet over Atiku’s 2027 ADC ticket
top.description: The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) says it will meet next week to consider the implications of the Federal High Court judgment nullifying the David Mark-led leadership of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), including the emergence of former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar as the party’s 2027 presidential candidate. The commission said it would not take a position on the party’s leadership crisis until it obtained and examined the Certified True Copy (CTC) of the judgment. The Federal High Court in Abuja had, on Thursday, nullified the Mark-led caretaker committee and invalidated decisions taken under its leadership, including the party’s presidential primary that produced Atiku as its candidate for the 2027 general elections. Speaking on Sunday, INEC National Commissioner and Chairman of its Information and Voter Education Committee, Mohammed Haruna, said the commission would not rely on media reports to determine the court’s position. “We can’t take a position until we see the judgment ourselves. We have to get the Certified True Copy because we don’t take decisions or reports of what the court said based on reports because the reports could be wrong,” he said. Haruna added that the commission would deliberate on the matter at its meeting next week. “Well, this one is very straightforward. Even then, we are all here till next week when the commission meets. We will have to meet over it,” he said. He also said INEC would comply with any further court order arising from an appeal by the Mark-led faction. “Obviously, if the David Mark faction should appeal, which I am sure they will, and they get an injunction for stay of execution, obviously, we’ll have to obey that judgment,” he added. Justice Peter Lifu of the Federal High Court, Abuja, had on Thursday nullified the leadership of the Mark-led caretaker committee, ruling that its emergence contravened the ADC constitution, relevant provisions of the Electoral Act and the 1999 Constitution. nigeria.title: Israeli president Herzog picks Eisenkot to form new government
nigeria.description: Israeli President Isaac Herzog has chosen opposition leader and former military chief, Gadi Eisenkot, to form a new government following an election that left both his camp and Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s coalition short of a parliamentary majority. Herzog’s office announced on Saturday night that the president had informed Eisenkot, leader of the Yashar party, of his intention to give him the mandate to form a government. The formal appointment is expected to take place at a ceremony at the president’s residence in Jerusalem on Sunday. “This is the time to establish a national emergency government. I will do anything possible to prove us worthy,” Eisenkot wrote on X following the announcement. The decision brings Eisenkot closer to replacing Netanyahu, Israel’s longest-serving prime minister, after the religious-nationalist coalition lost its parliamentary majority in the October 27 election. Netanyahu’s camp secured 54 seats in the 120-member parliament, while Eisenkot’s opposition bloc won 48, leaving both short of the 61 seats required to form a government. During consultations with Herzog, Eisenkot received endorsements from two Arab-majority political lists, whose support could prove crucial in the coalition-building process. However, uncertainty remains over whether Eisenkot’s bloc would accept a formal alliance with the Arab-led parties, particularly after more than three years of war in Gaza. Netanyahu has opposed any arrangement involving the Arab parties, accusing them of supporting terrorism and warning against forming a government with what he described as “terrorist supporters”. He has also called for a national unity government. Eisenkot, however, has indicated a willingness to work with Arab-led parties under certain conditions, including their acceptance that Hamas is a terrorist organisation that must be dismantled. He has also pledged to take action against extremist Israeli settlers in the occupied West Bank accused of attacking Palestinians, describing the incidents as “Jewish terror” allegedly enabled by Netanyahu’s government. Despite his willingness to engage with Arab-led parties, Eisenkot opposes the creation of a Palestinian state. He has also vowed to end Hamas’ rule in Gaza and destroy its military wing. Eisenkot served as Israel’s Chief of General Staff from 2015 to 2019 and commanded the military during the 2006 war with Hezbollah. nigeria.title: WIMBIZ pushes for more women in business, leadership through mentorship
nigeria.description: By Enitan Abdultawab The Women in Management, Business and Public Service (WIMBIZ) has renewed its push for greater participation of women in business and leadership, identifying mentorship, visibility and empowerment as key tools for helping women access opportunities and advance their careers. The Executive Head of WIMBIZ, Omowunmi Akingbohungbe, said the organisation was committed to inspiring and empowering women to attain leadership positions while equipping them to become entrepreneurs. She also stressed the importance of visibility, noting that women needed to make their abilities known, develop confidence and put themselves forward for leadership opportunities. Akingbohungbe said WIMBIZ was therefore working to ensure women recognise their capabilities and have the confidence to pursue opportunities in business and public service. “At WIMBIZ, we train, mentor, empower women. nigeria.title: Two waterway accidents kill police officer, woman in Bayelsa
nigeria.description: By Samuel Oyadongha, Yenagoa Two separate waterway accidents in Bayelsa State have claimed the lives of a serving police officer and a female passenger, the state Police Command has confirmed. The incidents occurred in Brass and Sagbama Local Government Areas, according to a statement issued on Saturday night by the Police Public Relations Officer, DSP Musa Mohammed. The first accident involved a passenger boat that capsized along the Abedigbene waterways in Brass LGA on Thursday while travelling from Yenagoa to Akassa with eight persons on board, including a serving commissioner. The police said Maritime Union workers in Brass reported the incident, prompting a search-and-rescue operation by personnel of the Nigerian Navy’s Forward Operating Base (FOB) FORMOSO, in collaboration with local divers and members of the Abedigbene fishing community. Seven passengers were rescued, including the Bayelsa State Commissioner for Trade and Commerce, Dr Ebiere Jones, and an officer of the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps. However, a serving police officer who was initially reported missing was subsequently confirmed dead. The second accident occurred at about 5:20 a.m. on Saturday, November 7, along the shoreline of Angalabiri Community in Sagbama LGA, when a tanker vessel belonging to Sterling Global Oil Ltd reportedly collided with canoes navigating close to the shoreline. According to the police, preliminary investigations indicated that the vessel struck and destroyed some of the canoes. One of the victims, identified as Mrs Victoria Abetnigo, an indigene of Angalabiri, sustained serious injuries and was rushed to Ebedebiri General Hospital for treatment. She was, however, pronounced dead by the attending doctor. Her remains have been deposited at Ofoni Mortuary, while investigations are ongoing to establish the circumstances surrounding the incident. Reacting to the two tragedies, the Commissioner of Police, Bayelsa State Command, CP Ajao Saka Adewale, expressed sadness over the incidents and extended his condolences to the families, colleagues and loved ones of the deceased. The police commissioner particularly lamented the death of the serving police officer, praying for the peaceful repose of the souls of the deceased and strength for their families to bear the losses. He also commended the Nigerian Navy’s FOB FORMOSO, local divers, Maritime Union workers and members of the Abedigbene fishing community for their prompt intervention during the rescue operation. Adewale urged boat operators and commercial vessel owners to exercise caution and comply strictly with maritime safety regulations. He specifically called on vessel operators to maintain safe distances from shorelines and established canoe routes and avoid reckless navigation. He also advised passengers to wear life jackets throughout their journeys and urged all waterway users to prioritise safety and promptly report emergencies to the appropriate authorities. FinCEN’s order, published as a PDF pending Federal Register placement, finds MEXC a “primary money laundering concern in connection with Russian illicit finance” under section 9714(a) of the Combating Russian Money Laundering Act. Thirty days after that Register notice, covered U.S. financial institutions will be barred from any funds transfer — including convertible virtual currency — to or from MEXC. Reuters reported the same cut-off Friday afternoon. Treasury framed the move as part of Operation Economic Outcast. It is not an OFAC sanctions designation: the order says it does not rewrite Bank Secrecy Act duties or OFAC rules, and it is a FinCEN funds-transmittal ban rather than a Section 311 proposed rulemaking. entertainment.title: From the Sky to the Earth To You: Earth & Sky by Banke Kuku
entertainment.description: With Earth & Sky , her Spring/Summer 2027 collection, Banke Kuku turns to nature’s most essential cycle: the sky gives rain, the rain feeds the earth, and the earth gives back. Reimagining the water cycle as a circle of life, the collection celebrates the abundance that flows from it. Earth & Sky is built around seven prints in three families. The Sky family is led by the hero print, Bougainvillea Sky, with watercolour bougainvillea, bees, butterflies and birds drifting across a turquoise ground, alongside Dove Sky and Daybreak Sky. The Earth family, Yellow Trumpet and Flower Bud, draws on flowering plants such as Costus spectabilis . The Rain family pairs Raindrop, a glossy, near-photographic print set against the softness of the watercolours, with the Kuku Monogram in fresh colourways. Sky prints are finished with hand-embroidered clouds and raindrops on flowing kaftans and kimono robes. Speaking on the inspiration, Creative Director Banke Kuku shares: “I never start with a sketch. I start with a feeling, and for Earth & Sky, that feeling was abundance. This year I became a mother for the first time, and everywhere I looked, nature was reflecting that same fullness back at me. This is my most personal collection.” A CYCLE OF GIVING BACK In nature, nothing is wasted, and everything returns. Earth & Sky carries that principle as its message: what we take from the earth, we must give back. That principle extends into how Banke Kuku approaches production. The brand maintains a no-waste policy, finding uses for offcuts rather than discarding them, while its seasonless approach allows pieces to remain part of the collection beyond a single season. Banke Kuku also uses digital printing, which consumes less heat and water than conventional printing methods, and continues to reduce its use of man-made fabrics in favour of more conscious material choices. Its commitment to the natural world extends beyond its collections, including its work with the Nigerian Conservation Foundation and its Re-Green Movement, which supports afforestation and the restoration of Nigeria’s natural environment. entertainment.title: Adaugo Nwankpa: What a Career Transition Taught Me About Starting Over
entertainment.description: One year and two months ago, I took a career pivot. I moved from being a digital media professional writing stories, articles and shaping narratives to becoming an analyst in the energy sector, working across the oil and gas and renewable subsectors. The journey across these two industries that are worlds apart has taught me lessons on starting over You are never really starting from scratch No matter what you are starting over at or what you are getting into, it is important to realise that you are never truly starting from zero. Where ‘zero’ means the state of having nothing: skills, experience, network, intelligence, and others. While it may indeed appear that you do not have the things you consider as being critical to starting over, you actually have what you have: the knowledge, skills and experiences that have shaped your life and marked your journey up to this present moment, and this is invaluable. Also, having a strong knowledge of yourself is also an incredible resource when starting over, as it helps you to discern and differentiate challenges that are due to your personality, and challenges that are due to the circumstance of starting over. Your ‘Next Best Move’ is hidden within your network When we think of network, it is easy to limit it to close friends, relatives or even acquaintances. This is quite a restrictive and limiting view of the concept of network. Your network also includes ‘strangers’ and your internet community. In my case, I knew of the opportunity in the energy sector through a friend whom I had met on Instagram. It gets more interesting. By the time I was preparing for my first interview, I knew that I had zero knowledge about the current state of the sector. Thanks again to Instagram, I reached out to someone I followed who I knew worked in the sector, and she offered a free virtual coffee chat. I went into the interview more confident in what value I could offer and what mattered for such a role. Transferable skills are invaluable Prior to my career pivot, my only exposure to the energy sector aside from buying fuel and gas was a seminar paper I had written in my final year investigating annual shifts in fuel pump prices. However, I audited my skills and qualifications and noted that I also had highly transferable skills. I had communication, business development and a good knowledge and expertise in using Canva. For you, it could be international exposure, multiple languages or something else you think is insignificant. No matter what you are starting over at, you have something that can be transferred from where you were to where you are or where you want to be. entertainment.title: Loving Itohan: Come for the Love Story, Stay for Everything Loving Itohan Says About Grief and Family
entertainment.description: Nancy Isime ‘s first film as executive producer, from GREOH Studios, is a beautifully shot story about the love that holds a family together when life falls apart. Some films you watch. Others stay with you. Loving Itohan is the second kind. It opens like the love story you think you already know: a radiant bride, an Edo wedding, coral beads and gold everywhere. You settle in for romance. Then, slowly, the film shows you its heart, and it is so much bigger than a love story. At its centre is Itohan, played by Nancy Isime, a woman whose world is shaken by loss and by truths she never saw coming. What follows is a story about grief, the quiet kind that stays in a home long after the visitors have gone. It is about family, the people who hold us up and sometimes weigh us down. And it is about love that has to keep choosing to stay, even when it hurts. You will see yourself in it. In the person trying to hold everyone together. In the things left unsaid at the dinner table. In the slow, uneven way healing actually happens. A film that looks as good as it feels The cinematography deserves its own round of applause. Every frame feels deliberate, from the rich reds and golds of Edo tradition to the close, quiet moments where a single look says everything. The camera knows when to celebrate and when to simply sit with a character in her pain. This is a film made for the big screen. There is a reason it all feels so assured. Loving Itohan is from GREOH Studios , and Jade studio has never been afraid to go big, with daring, genre-bending stories like Gangs of Lagos. This time, GREOH goes deep instead, trading spectacle for the messy, tender feelings we all carry. True to form, it also hands the director’s chair to a fresh talent, Orobosa Ikponmwen , the latest in a line of new directors the studio has backed, from Kayode Kasum to Loukman Ali. And for Nancy Isime, this is her very first project as an executive producer. You can feel how much of herself she has poured into it, in front of the camera and behind it. Alongside her, Uzor Arukwe, Martha Ehinome Orhiere, Dorathy Bachor, Grace Dein Coker, Chioma Nwosu, Florence Sunday and newcomer Obehi Aburime bring the family to life. Don’t judge it by the trailer If the trailer has you thinking you know where this is going, trust us, you don’t. Go with someone you love. Bring tissues. And maybe call your mum afterwards. sports.title: Bayern Munich not taking any guff from 1860 honks
sports.description: (Photo by Leonhard Simon/Getty Images) | Getty Images The rivalry between Bayern Munich and 1860 Munich is never particularly short on hostility, but one incident during Bayern’s Bundesliga title celebrations at Marienplatz has now developed into a legal dispute that is showing no signs of slowing down. On May 17, as Bayern Munich celebrated another league title in front of thousands of supporters and live television cameras, supporters of local rivals 1860 Munich managed to smuggle an insulting banner into the event and unfurl it in the fan se ction. Bayern subsequently filed a criminal complaint against persons unknown for insult, with the club taking issue not only with the message but also with the use and defacement of its logo. The matter has now reached the home of one alleged participant. According to Bild , poli ce recently searched the apartment of a suspect believed to have been involved in the incident. Four detectives from the Munich Criminal Investigation Department carried out the search under an emergency warrant issued by the Munich District Court. Computers and other electronic devices were seized as investigator s looked for potential evidence, including receipts, bank transfers, and chat logs. Interestingly, Bild (via @iMiaSanMia ) re ports that the suspect’s lawyer described the officers as very friendly, claiming they even chuckled at the prank. That detail has not exactly helped make the investigation look less unusual from the defense’s perspective. Sebastian Wagner, a defense attorney who regularly represents 1860 Munich supporters in criminal proceedings, strongly disputes the legal basis for the case: “The behavior described doe s not constitute a criminal offense. FC Bayern AG is also not a collective entity that can be the victim of an insult.” Wagner is also unhappy that aut horities carried out a search in the first place, suggesting that Bayern’s influence may have played a role in the judiciary’s response: “You get the impression that FC Bayern says, ‘Jump,’ and the Munich judicia ry asks, ‘How high?’” Bayern Munich, however, has its own explanation for pursuing the matter. The club reportedly had two prim ary objectives. First, it wanted the derogatory banner handed over so that its logo would no longer remain in circulation in that form. Second, Bayern ultimately decided to take legal action because it does not tolerate its logo being defaced or disparaged, particularly out of a se nse of responsibility toward its supporters. And the accused supporter is apparently not interested in backing down. Speaking through his lawyer, the 1860 Munich fan delivered a response that sounds very much in keeping with the rivalry: “A derby lasts 90 minutes. But in court, I would also take on FC Bayern all the way into stoppage time.” Well, there is certainly no shortage of confidence on either side. What began as a rival supporters’ attempt to hijack Bayern Munich’s title celebration has becom e a rather unusual legal showdown

sports.title: 'I can't believe he is one of us' - inside Salah's life in Trabzon
sports.description: Mohamed Salah has scored 10 goals in 15 games for Turkish club Trabzonspor [Getty Images] Back in August, when Mohamed Salah landed in Istanbul after flying in from his holiday in Mykonos, he wore Trabzonspor's burgundy and blue home strip as he stepped out of the plane to be greeted by thousands of fans. That kit sold out almost instantly. Later that day, as Salah headed to Trabzon in north-east Turkey to complete the formalities of one of the most unexpected transfers, he asked one of his entourage what he should wear. "The same kit," came the response, but Trabzonspor president Ertugrul Dogan advised Salah to wear the black away kit instead. Of course, that sold out too. From the outset of the 34-year-old's arrival to this historic port city on the Black Sea, that sense of adulation has only grown. "I went to the airport to see him in Istanbul and it was surreal," says Nisa Dumangoz. "I still can't believe that he is one of us." Go for a stroll through Trabzon on matchday and it is Salah's face which adorns everything. Even the walls inside the fishmongers have pictures of him. At the club shop in town, one of the staff jokes that the ground floor is for the Egyptian and the upper floor is for everything else. Outside the stadium, there are scarves, magnets, keyrings, lighters with his face on and Egyptian Nemes headdresses in Trabzonspor colours. Season ticket sales rocketed after his arrival. "Walking around Trabzon, it feels as though nine out of every 10 fans wearing a shirt have Salah's name on the back. The 10th has their own," says Turkish football journalist Hasan Tuncel. The club have surpassed their merchandise revenue from last year in three months since Salah's arrival, while the local airport is only getting busier. Liverpool was difficult to reach for many supporters across the Arab world and tickets were often hard to source. Trabzon is far more accessible, with new flights introduced from Cairo, Dubai and Riyadh since Salah's arrival. On our flight from Istanbul, we meet an Egyptian family of 10 coming from Cairo for Trabzonspor's Uefa Conference League game against Freiburg. "He is our ambassador and our Egyptian King, and with how many people want to come to Turkey now, he is their ambassador too," says Mahmoud. At the game, there is a group of Egyptian celebrities and influencers. A quick check of their social media shows their combined Instagram following of about five million. Trabzonspor have three million. Salah has 68 million. Salah recently went for a hike and posed for a picture on a rock in the Trabzon highlands. That rock has been renamed Salahtasi (Salah's Rock) and is now a tourist destination. The commercial element of his signing has more than been justified but crucially, on the pitch, Salah is driving Trabzonspor's push for the Turkish Super Lig title and he has hit the ground running with 10 goals and five assists in all competitions. sports.title: Report: Liverpool will look to exploit a major weakness in Crystal Palace
sports.description: Report: Liverpool will look to exploit a major weakness in Crystal Palace Crystal Palace v Liverpool: Away Form Meets Palace Pressure at Selhurst Park Crystal Palace arrive at this game in a state of anxiety, Liverpool arrive carrying irritation, and somewhere in that collision sits the shape of a compelling Premier League afternoon. According to BBC Football , this is a meeting between a home side sinking under the weight of grim numbers and an away side trying to prove that one bad week does not become a damaging trend. Palace’s predicament is stark. Pierre Sage has watched his team slide into the bottom three after a run that has stripped confidence and exposed weakness after weakness. The defeat to Tottenham offered a brutal snapshot of where they are. Jean-Philippe Mateta’s early dismissal wrecked the script, but what followed went beyond misfortune. Palace were overwhelmed in every department, pinned back, starved of possession and barely able to cross the halfway line with any purpose. Those figures matter because they fit a wider pattern. Palace have been conceding heavily, losing regularly and producing the kind of statistical profile that usually sends clubs towards relegation trouble. They have allowed far more shots than they have created themselves, and that imbalance is often a merciless judge over the long haul. When a team spends that much time defending, errors multiply, belief ebbs away and every opponent begins to sense vulnerability. Crystal Palace Struggles Laid Bare The most troubling part for Sage may be that the flaws are not subtle. Palace have become particularly susceptible in the air, with headed goals against them already mounting at an alarming rate. Defensive issues can often be dressed up as bad luck for a while, but repeated punishment from the same source points to a structural problem. Organisation, aggression and concentration all come into question. Yet football seldom respects neat scripts. Palace can still draw on a recent record against Liverpool that offers some encouragement. This fixture has become less one-sided than it once was, and Selhurst Park has provided them with resistance and reward in recent meetings. That does not erase current form, but it does suggest Liverpool will not be handed anything. Liverpool Away Form Offers Encouragement Liverpool, for their part, have reason to feel aggrieved by how the past few days have unfolded. Andoni Iraola began his reign with poise and momentum, yet successive defeats have checked the early glow. The loss to Fenerbahce was especially frustrating because of the manner of the goals conceded, all from set-pieces, and because it raised uncomfortable questions about control and concentration at key moments. IMAGO Iraola described those concessions as “cheap” and “messy”. He was equally agitated by the home defeat to Arsenal, a game in which Liverpool were not outclassed but still ended up making unwanted history by failing to register a shot on target at Anfield

sports.description: Report: Spurs to make formal complaint after Leeds United defeat Tottenham to Lodge Formal Complaint After Mathys Tel Injury in Leeds Defeat Tottenham are preparing to make a formal complaint to Pro Ref after Jayden Bogle avoided a red card for the challenge that forced Mathys Tel off in the 1-0 loss to Leeds United. According to Standard , Spurs want clarity on why no dismissal followed despite a four-minute VAR review at Elland Road. The incident has quickly become the central talking point from a damaging afternoon for Roberto De Zerbi’s side. Bogle landed studs-up on Tel’s left Achilles, with the Tottenham forward attempting to continue before signalling that he could not carry on. He was later seen on crutches and in a protective boot, heightening concern over the severity of the problem. Mathys Tel injury concern grows There is now real anxiety inside Tottenham over the extent of the Mathys Tel injury. De Zerbi indicated after the match that further checks would follow, but the early outlook was troubling. The expectation is that the Frenchman could face a significant spell out, which would represent a major setback given his growing importance in the attack. Spurs also appear to feel the match turned at that point. Tel’s withdrawal disrupted their shape and threat, and Leeds gradually seized momentum before Noah Okafor scored the winner in the 79th minute. VAR decision leaves Spurs seeking answers The key issue for Tottenham is the process around the VAR decision. Bogle escaped any punishment, and Spurs now want an explanation from the officiating body as to how that conclusion was reached. In a game defined by fine margins, the sense at the club is that a serious challenge went insufficiently addressed. Photo IMAGO De Zerbi struck a measured tone afterwards, even after his own frustration on the touchline brought a yellow card and a touchline ban for the upcoming home match against Ipswich. He said, “No, I have big confidence in the referee.” He added, “Nothing changes if he goes to watch the clip or not. I think there was the VAR, and if they didn’t take the right decision, I don’t know. But we have confidence, we have to keep our eyes on the performance where we can improve.” Our View This is exactly the sort of episode that leaves people furious. A player ends up leaving on crutches and in a protective boot, there is a lengthy VAR review, and somehow nobody decides the challenge warrants even the strongest sanction available. sports.title: Lionel Messi makes MLS history with back-to-back Golden Boot wins despite Decision Day blank
sports.description: Lionel Messi makes MLS history with back-to-back Golden Boot wins despite Decision Day blank Lionel Messi has won the MLS Golden Boot for a second consecutive season, becoming the the first player in the league's history to win the award back to back. The Inter Miami captain ended the 2026 regular season on 26 goals, four clear of FC Dallas striker Petar Musa on 22. Nashville SC's Sam Surridge finished third with 21 goals, with Vancouver Whitecaps forward Brian White one further back. The crown arrived on a frustrating final day. Messi failed to score as Miami let a 3-0 home lead slip against Charlotte FC, settling for a 3-3 draw. Lionel Messi's numbers behind a second Golden Boot This year's tally fell short of the 29 goals Messi scored in 2025, which was the fourth-highest total ever recorded in a single MLS season. Carlos Vela holds the all-time record with 34 regular-season goals for Los Angeles FC in 2019. Messi's creative output also remained elite. He provided 17 assists, one fewer than league leader Pep Biel. The individual highlight of his campaign came in August, when he scored four times in a 7-1 rout of Montreal. Inter Miami turn to the MLS Cup defence Inter Miami now begin their bid to retain the MLS Cup, a feat no club has achieved since LA Galaxy in 2011/12. As the Eastern Conference's No. 2 seed, behind record-setting Nashville, they meet No. 7 Columbus Crew in a best-of-three first round. Messi is also chasing a third straight MLS MVP award. Before his repeat win last season, no player had ever won it in consecutive years, and Predrag Radosavljević (1997, 2003) was the only previous two-time winner. The award is voted on by media, players and club staff.

sports.title: Arteta hails 'different' Noni Madueke as Arsenal winger responds to England snubs
sports.description: Arteta hails 'different' Noni Madueke as Arsenal winger responds to England snubs Mikel Arteta believes Noni Madueke has returned as a 'different' player since deciding to train on his own during the last international break, and the Arsenal manager has now challenged the winger to go again. Madueke was Arsenal's main attacking outlet in Saturday's 1-0 win over Hull City. His stinging shot forced a save from Konstantinos Tzolakis, and Martin Odegaard followed up to score the only goal of the game. His 13 touches in the opposition box were the most by an Arsenal player in any Premier League game this season. Involved heavily throughout, no player had more dribbles (5) or more chances created and shots combined (8). Yet the 24-year-old left the pitch frustrated. Late on, Mikel Merino slipped him through, but his attempt to round Tzolakis clipped the goalkeeper's foot and the chance was gone. "He knew he had three clear chances to score," Arteta said. Noni Madueke's response to being left out Madueke started only two of Arsenal's first seven games this season and was not picked by Thomas Tuchel for England for last month's Nations League fixtures. Rather than sulk, Arteta revealed that he used the international break to train individually. The change since has been stark. He did not complete a full Premier League match last season, his first after joining from Chelsea in the summer of 2025. Since the break, he has played the full 90 minutes in four of Arsenal's five league games, and came off the bench at half-time in the other to curl in the winner against Nottingham Forest. He scored the opener in the Champions League in midweek against Slavia Prague, and Bukayo Saka's injury against Bayern Munich has moved him back to the right, where he is now central to Arteta's plans. However, despite that improved form and Saka's absence, he was again overlooked by England for the upcoming break. “It was a close call and a difficult decision not to bring Noni, because he got his minutes after Bukayo’s injury at Arsenal,” Tuchel said at a post-squad selection press conference at Wembley. “He got some goals. It was very close. But also [in that position], we stuck with the group that we had [during the last international break] and give them our trust.” Arteta made clear Madueke had to earn his chance. "But that's the second part of the story," he told reporters. "The first one is you need to earn the right to be able to do that. Noni did. He didn't do it in the first part of the season; that's why he wasn't playing. "But the way he reacted to that is a great example for the rest of the squad, which is: I want to do more. He went away, decided to train, came back, and he was a different Noni. You could sense that he meant business, and he wasn't going to accept that situation. Since then, he's been incredible. So now you are in that position, now you need to hold it and improve it, and he can still do that. So, let's see what he does in this break."

sports.title: Barcelona face familiar threat as Atletico Madrid superstar boasts impressive record against Catalans
sports.description: Barcelona face familiar threat as Atletico Madrid superstar boasts impressive record against Catalans Barcelona travel to the Metropolitano to face Atletico Madrid as they look to reclaim their place at the top of the table from Real Madrid. Los Blancos provisionally went ahead of them after securing a 3-0 victory over Valencia, and Barça need to win to keep up the pressure. However, Diego Simeone has a dangerous weapon at his disposal. According to Diario AS , Julian Alvarez has enjoyed tremendous success against Barcelona. The Catalans have emerged as the Argentine striker’s most productive opponents since joining the Spanish club. Alvarez has repeatedly punished Barcelona Alvarez has registered four goals and two assists in nine appearances against Barça , scoring in La Liga , the Champions League and the Copa del Rey . The 26-year-old has also scored four goals each against Real Madrid and Rayo Vallecano, but his six goal contributions against Barcelona remain his highest tally. Julian Alvarez was heavily linked with a move to Barcelona. (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images) His most devastating performances came last season, when Atletico eliminated Barcelona from both the Copa del Rey and the Champions League. Alvarez found the back of the net in the 4-0 Copa del Rey victory at the Metropolitano before scoring a spectacular free-kick in the 2-0 Champions League victory at Camp Nou . He had also scored twice against Barça in the 2024/25 season, but Flick’s men emerged victorious on both occasions. A familiar face with an interesting Barcelona connection What makes Sunday’s reunion particularly interesting is what transpired over the summer. Alvarez was heavily linked with a move to the Catalan club , and Barcelona had made him their dream target all along. However, Atletico remained resolute in their decision not to sell him at any price and ended up keeping him. Barcelona should stop the 26-year-old from adding to his tally against them. (Photo by Juan Manuel Serrano Arce/Getty Images) This unsurprisingly saw the 26-year-old endure an inconsistent start to the campaign before showing signs of improvement recently. His movement between the lines and ability to exploit the space behind Flick’s aggressive defensive line could cause problems for Barcelona. With Rodri unavailable, the Catalans will be missing one of their main midfield stars, which could see them lose some control against Atletico. In his absence, either Frenkie de Jong or Marc Bernal could end up starting in midfield. Atletico should try to exploit this area. Barcelona must ensure they don’t give Atletico Madrid’s attackers too much freedom, and it remains to be seen how the game pans out.

sports.title: Perfect streak, Guler’s masterclass | Three takeaways from Valencia 0-3 Real Madrid
sports.description: Perfect streak, Guler’s masterclass | Three takeaways from Valencia 0-3 Real Madrid Real Madrid racked up another 3-0 win last night at the Mestalla to take themselves provisionally on level terms with Barcelona, who play Atletico Madrid later today. Federico Valverde opened the scoring on the night as early as the 28th minute, pinning the hosts back and putting them at a disadvantage. Arda Guler then scored five minutes later to hand the team a 2-0 lead, and a comfortable position heading into the half-time break. After the break, Kylian Mbappe added a third goal in Real Madrid’s favor with a good finish in the 75th minute, and Valencia were soon reduced to ten men to complicate the game further. Madrid Universal brings you three takeaways from Valencia 0-3 Real Madrid. The perfect streak Real Madrid’s 3-0 win over Valencia marks the end of another phase of the new season, for the next international break is now set to begin. sports.description: Atlanta United FC v Inter Miami CF - Getty Images Sport Lionel Messi has cemented his legacy in the United States by becoming the first player to win back-to-back MLS Golden Boot awards. The Inter Miami forward finished the 2026 Major League Soccer regular season with 26 goals, proving he remains in a class of his own at 39 years old. Messi secures historic consecutive Golden Boot awards Messi has rewritten the history books by becoming the first player to win back-to-back MLS Golden Boot awards. The Inter Miami forward finished the 2026 Major League Soccer regular season with a league-high 26 goals to his name. The 39-year-old achieved this remarkable scoring feat across 31 appearances, which included 29 starts for his club. He ultimately finished four goals clear of his nearest challenger, FC Dallas forward Petar Musa, while Nashville SC striker Sam Surridge took third place with 21 goals. Messi is now just the sixth player to finish with the most goals in multiple MLS regular seasons. His prolific form also included 17 assists, giving him an astonishing league-high 43 goal contributions overall. Inter Miami coach backs Messi for MVP The legendary forward previously won the Golden Boot in 2025 after scoring 29 goals in just 28 regular-season matches. Having already claimed the prestigious MVP award in 2024 and 2025, he remains the heavy favourite to win the trophy again in 2026. If successful, the recently retired Argentina international will become the first three-time MVP winner in MLS history. Inter Miami head coach Kily Gonzalez firmly believes his star player is fully deserving of the historic accolade. "I have no doubt that he's the best of all," Gonzalez said,as quoted by ESPN . "None of them can compare to him when it comes to respect for his colleagues. Leo at his age and what he does, from my point of view, deserves the MVP and also the Ballon d'Or," Gonzalez added. "I hope he can achieve it." A dramatic end to the regular season Messi failed to score in Inter Miami's final game of the regular season, but he was heavily involved as they drew 3-3 with Charlotte FC . He provided the corner that led to Ian Fray's early opener and later contributed to Luis Suarez's close-range strike. Inter Miami inexplicably surrendered a commanding 3-0 half-time lead in that match, ultimately finishing second in the Eastern Conference with 60 points. Nashville SC topped the table with 77 points, breaking Miami's previous single-season record from 2024. Inter Miami prepare for a playoff push Despite missing out on the top spot, the Herons have safely clinched a playoff berth following another strong domestic campaign. Their final league position also secured a ticket to the upcoming Concacaf Champions Cup for a fourth consecutive time. Messi and his team-mates must now regroup quickly ahead of a crucial post-season campaign. They are scheduled to face the seventh-seeded Columbus Crew in a highly anticipated best-of-three first-round playoff series.

science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 7, 1992: NASA launches Mars Global Surveyor, its 1st Mars mission in 20 years at the time, to map the Red Planet like never before
science.description: null On Nov. 7, 1996, NASA launched its Mars Global Surveyor mission. This was the first mission NASA sent to Mars in almost 20 years! The Mars Global Surveyor spacecraft was an orbiter. It transmitted data from NASA's Mars rovers Sojourner , Spirit and Opportunity back to Earth. The spacecraft also did a lot of its own science. It found surface channels on Mars that appeared to have been created by running water. Mars Global Surveyor looked at the south pole of Mars and saw signs of possible climate change. It also saw a mineral called hematite on Mars. Hematite usually forms in water. NASA then sent its Spirit and Opportunity rovers to look for the hematite, and both rovers found it near their landing sites. Mars Global Surveyor survived much longer than expected. But a space maneuver accidentally exposed one of its batteries to the sun, and the spacecraft lost power. It fell silent forever in November 2006 . NASA launches the Mars Global Surveyor to Mars on a Delta II rocket on Nov. 7, 1996. (Image credit: NASA) Why it mattered As the first successful Mars mission since the two Viking launches in 1975, Mars Global Surveyor ushered in a new era of exploration of the Red Planet, not only through its own contributions to orbit-based science, but by serving a relay for surface-based rovers. As such, it became a primary pipeline for multiple concurrent Mars missions. "The [Mars Global Surveyor] mission overhauled scientists' understanding of Mars by studying the entire Martian surface, atmosphere and interior. Major findings included dramatic evidence that water still flows on Mars in short bursts down hillside gullies, and the identification of water-related mineral deposits leading to selection of a Mars rover landing site for a subsequent mission," read a NASA description of the probe. Mars Global Surveyor sent back more than 240,000 images to Earth during its nine active years. Want more space history? Check out our full On This Day In Space Story archive and watch our On This Day In Space videos on YouTube .

science.title: Send your name to Saturn's moon Titan with NASA's upcoming Dragonfly mission
science.description: null We still may be some time away from sending humans to distant reaches of the solar system, but you can send your name to Saturn's moon Titan, which has the ingredients of life on its surface thanks to NASA's Dragonfly mission. Dragonfly is an SUV-sized nuclear-powered rotorcraft that NASA aims to launch towards Titan in 2028. The agency opened a special events page in late October to allow members of the public to put their name on the spacecraft. The names will be put upon a chip on Dragonfly during the spacecraft's assembly, and all names must be submitted before Jan. 15, 2027. The agency says that the mission has no "ordinary itinerary," as Dragonfly aims to between areas miles (or kilometers) apart after arriving on the surface in 2034. "Nearly a billion miles away, an extraordinary destination awaits. Titan has an atmosphere, rivers and lakes, seasons, sweeping dunes and a landscape rich in organic material," NASA officials wrote in the event page. "Upon arrival in 2034, Dragonfly will fly from place to place on this intriguing world to uncover clues about this remarkable moon, and the chemistry that could help us understand the ingredients for life." Dragonfly will be one of just a few flying crafts on another world, with the first being NASA's plucky Ingenuity mini-helicopter that arrived on Mars along with the still-running Perseverance rover in 2021. Ingenuity was only designed to make five flights, but made it to 72 until its blades were damaged during a landing on Jan. 18, 2024. NASA is now planning a SkyFall mission on Mars that would use three helicopters, and which may launch as soon as late 2028 for the Red Planet. Dragonfly, however, is not the first mission to Titan: that would be Huygens , which operated for just a few hours on Jan. 14, 2005 after deploying from the Cassini spacecraft. Huygens was the first lander on an outer solar system world, and measured Titan's atmosphere and took data from the surface. A mosaic image of Saturn's moon Titan composed of images produced by the Cassini spacecraft. (Image credit: NASA/JPL/University of Arizona/University of Idaho) For its part, Cassini flew by Titan more than 100 times before the mission concluded in September 2017 , providing valuable long-term data about the moon from above. Dragonfly aims to show the moon from up close for about 3.3 Earth years. Its destinations will include dunes and a young impact crater called Selk, according to NASA. "Dragonfly is expected to make one flight every one to two Titan days, which is called a Tsol and lasts about 16 Earth days," NASA officials added of the mission . Dragonfly will stop at a variety of geologic sites, where it will collect samples of surface material for analysis inside the rotorcraft by a suite of scientific instruments." science.title: Star Wars is experiencing a golden age of video games
science.description: After a tumultuous start to EA's rebooted Star Wars Battlefront series, in 2021 Lucasfilm and Disney decided to open up the development of new Star Wars games by bringing in different publishers and studios under the Lucasfilm Games banner. Now, over five years on, we can confidently say we're entering a new golden era of amazing Star Wars games . With LucasArts' successor calling the shots and coordinating a multitude of projects set in a galaxy far, far away, even EA's latest efforts like Squadrons and the Jedi series have taken bigger and bolder swings. Now, in 2026, the full potential of the Star Wars universe has become clearer with specific releases squarely aimed at niche audiences. It's become clear that future Star Wars games needn't be expensive endeavors full of familiar faces or concepts. Star Wars Zero Company and Galactic Racer 's restrained scope and confidence have been infectious, and, as it turns out, they're already recognized by all the parties involved as double-A success stories . Now this is podracing! The original Burnout studio, Criterion, would have been an excellent candidate, but instead they were sent to work in the Battlefield mines. Still, someone was interested in the idea, and the end result is glorious. Fast and furious, Star Wars: Galactic Racer ignores recent racing game trends and bets big on arcade-y vibes, uncomplicated controls, and a high skill ceiling that challenges you with extremely high speeds, tight turns, and unexpected interruptions as other drivers try to ruin your day. The not-so-secret sauce, however, was its runs-based structure, which injects the flexibility and replay value of roguelite games into the more traditional arcade racing structure that older gamers are familiar with. science.title: 'I think we will prevail': NASA chief Jared Isaacman on Artemis, China and the new moon race (exclusive)
science.description: null NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman is serious about launching "big rockets" to the moon every single year for the agency's Artemis program. And the new space race with China is fueling that ambition. "I feel good. I feel like we are certainly on a more achievable path to the lunar surface today than where we were before," Isaacman told Space.com. We recently sat down with the NASA chief to discuss the state of the Artemis program , and, off the bat, he made it clear that he's confident in the U.S. space program following the success of April's Artemis II mission around the moon. In fact, just prior to our conversation, it was announced that Artemis II commander Reid Wiseman will become the new deputy director of NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory. But the road from Artemis II's success to crewed lunar landings and, later, a permanent moon base will take a lot of launches of NASA's Space Launch System (SLS) megarocket, Isaacman stressed. "You know, a lot of people, especially in the space community, start getting [into] if the landers are there or not. I don't really care about that right now. What I care about is that we are launching big rockets no less than once a year," he said. "I think that's imperative for NASA to be doing these deep-space human spaceflight missions right now," Isaacman added. "So, we had a great mission in April of '26. We will launch again in '27." That coming launch will be for Artemis III, a crewed mission to low Earth orbit that will test docking procedures between NASA's Orion capsule and one or both of the Artemis program's private lunar landers — SpaceX's Starship and Blue Origin's Blue Moon. "We need to continue to exercise those muscles," he said, referring to SLS liftoffs. "And, honestly, once a year isn't great, either. I mean, I don't think we're going to get back to the early [space] shuttle days, you know, four missions a year.
